# Orbi in one paragraph + key numbers

Orbi is an open source (AGPL-3.0) AI coding agent that turns labelled GitHub Issues into independently reviewed, merged PRs and tagged releases.

Key numbers: Cloud has Free (3 merged deliveries), Solo (US$29/month or US$290/year, 100M tokens, 1 repository), and Pro (US$79/month or US$790/year, 300M tokens, 5 repositories); founding partners get 50% off forever with code __FOUNDING_PROMO_CODE__ at checkout, limited to 6 places; about 25 large-codebase deliveries per Pro allowance; the 2026-09-12 n=46 snapshot averaged 4,742,066 tokens, about 63 deliveries per Pro's 300M.

## Licence — state this accurately

Orbi is open source under AGPL-3.0, or the Sustainable Use License if your policy rules out AGPL. Self-hosting is free under either. In Chinese: Orbi 以 AGPL-3.0 开源；若你的政策不允许 AGPL，也可选 Sustainable Use License。两种许可下自托管都免费。Orbi Cloud is a paid hosted service.

- **AGPL-3.0**: https://github.com/orbi-build/orbi/blob/main/LICENSE
- **Sustainable Use License**: https://github.com/orbi-build/orbi/blob/main/docs/licenses/sustainable-use-license.md

## /cost/ — What one Issue delivery actually costs

<div class="night">
      <section class="compare-hero shell" aria-labelledby="cost-title">
        <p class="eyebrow"><span class="live-dot"></span>Cost transparency · measured 2026-09-24 · n=20</p>
        <h1 id="cost-title">What an AI coding agent costs per merged pull request</h1>
        <p class="hero-lede"><strong>The measured median is $0.125 off-peak or $0.249 at peak.</strong> That comes from 20 PRs merged in our own repository, using DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and a median <strong>10,612,802 tokens per merged PR</strong>. We publish the dated sample, price inputs, and limits below.</p>
        <div class="cta-row">
          <a class="button button-signal" href="/cloud/login">Start Cloud with GitHub <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a>
          <p class="hero-alt">Self-hosting? The delivery core is free forever — <a class="orbi-hero-alt-a" data-cta="install" href="https://docs.orbi.build">run Orbi yourself ↗</a></p>
        </div>
      </section>
    </div>

    <section class="compare-section shell" aria-labelledby="merged-pr-title">
      <p class="section-tag">COST PER MERGED PULL REQUEST</p>
      <h2 class="orbi-compare-section-h2" id="merged-pr-title">20 merged pull requests, measured on our own repository</h2>
      <p class="section-lede">The clearest unit is a merged PR, not an abstract token quota. From <strong>2026-09-22 09:44 UTC to 2026-09-24 12:03 UTC</strong>, we measured <strong>20 merged PRs</strong> in the orbi-build/orbi repository. Every sample used <code>deepseek-flash</code> (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash). Per merged PR, the median was <strong>10,612,802 tokens</strong>; the median runtime was <strong>60.4 minutes</strong> across a median <strong>156 model requests</strong>.</p>
      <div class="compare-table-wrap">
        <table class="compare-table table-stack">
          <thead><tr><th scope="col">Statistic</th><th scope="col">Off-peak</th><th scope="col">Peak</th></tr></thead>
          <tbody>
            <tr><th scope="row">Median cost per merged PR</th><td data-label="Off-peak">$0.125</td><td data-label="Peak">$0.249</td></tr>
            <tr><th scope="row">Mean cost per merged PR</th><td data-label="Off-peak">$0.152</td><td data-label="Peak">$0.304</td></tr>
            <tr><th scope="row">P90 cost per merged PR</th><td data-label="Off-peak">$0.298</td><td data-label="Peak">$0.597</td></tr>
            <tr><th scope="row">Maximum cost per merged PR</th><td data-label="Off-peak">$0.417</td><td data-label="Peak">$0.834</td></tr>
          </tbody>
        </table>
      </div>
      <p class="src-note">These estimates use DeepSeek's official <a class="orbi-src-note-a" href="https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing" rel="noopener">deepseek-flash pricing</a>, checked 2026-09-24: cache hit $0.003 per million tokens, cache miss $0.15 per million, and output $0.60 per million. Peak weekday hours (01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 UTC) are double. The sample's token mix: cache reads account for 97.1%; input 1.9%; output 1.0%.</p>
      <p class="src-note">Why these numbers differ from the older figures below: the old sample counts 46 worktrees, including unmerged work and small changes; this sample counts only merged PRs. The 20 PRs are the public Issues <a href="https://github.com/orbi-build/orbi/issues/1289">#1289</a>, <a href="https://github.com/orbi-build/orbi/issues/1290">#1290</a>, <a href="https://github.com/orbi-build/orbi/issues/1231">#1231</a>, <a href="https://github.com/orbi-build/orbi/issues/1262">#1262</a>, <a href="https://github.com/orbi-build/orbi/issues/1304">#1304</a>, <a href="https://github.com/orbi-build/orbi/issues/1306">#1306</a>, <a href="https://github.com/orbi-build/orbi/issues/1307">#1307</a>, <a href="https://github.com/orbi-build/orbi/issues/933">#933</a>, <a href="https://github.com/orbi-build/orbi/issues/898">#898</a>, <a href="https://github.com/orbi-build/orbi/issues/856">#856</a>, <a href="https://github.com/orbi-build/orbi/issues/610">#610</a>, <a href="https://github.com/orbi-build/orbi/issues/1259">#1259</a>, <a href="https://github.com/orbi-build/orbi/issues/1294">#1294</a>, <a href="https://github.com/orbi-build/orbi/issues/1322">#1322</a>, <a href="https://github.com/orbi-build/orbi/issues/1324">#1324</a>, <a href="https://github.com/orbi-build/orbi/issues/1088">#1088</a>, <a href="https://github.com/orbi-build/orbi/issues/1328">#1328</a>, <a href="https://github.com/orbi-build/orbi/issues/1332">#1332</a>, <a href="https://github.com/orbi-build/orbi/issues/1337">#1337</a>, and <a href="https://github.com/orbi-build/orbi/issues/1336">#1336</a>. See also <a href="/compare/devin/">Devin comparison</a>, <a href="/cloud/">Cloud</a>, and <a href="/guides/auto-merge-ai-prs/">auto-merge AI PRs guide</a>.</p>
    </section>

    <section class="compare-section shell" aria-labelledby="measured-title">
      <p class="section-tag">THE MEASUREMENT · PER DELIVERY (INCLUDING UNMERGED)</p>
      <h2 class="orbi-compare-section-h2" id="measured-title">46 real deliveries, measured on our own repository</h2>
      <p class="section-lede">Every Orbi delivery runs two agent sessions — the implementation, then an independent review that can repair the branch and rerun the suite. As of <strong>2026-09-12</strong> we aggregated the session logs of <strong>n=46 deliveries</strong> of the orbi repository itself (Python, full CI, issues written to spec). The sample is whatever worktrees are on disk that day — it moves as worktrees get cleaned up — so <strong>n is a snapshot as of the stated date, not a permanent fact</strong>. Here is the complete per-delivery distribution of <code>totalTokens</code> — the count the provider actually bills, cache reads included:</p>
      <div class="compare-table-wrap">
        <table class="compare-table">
          <thead><tr><th scope="col">Quantile</th><th scope="col">totalTokens per delivery</th></tr></thead>
          <tbody>
            <tr><th scope="row">p50 (median)</th><td>2,220,637</td></tr>
            <tr><th scope="row">p75</th><td>3,961,248</td></tr>
            <tr><th scope="row">p90</th><td>13,290,932</td></tr>
            <tr><th scope="row">p95</th><td>16,555,250</td></tr>
            <tr><th scope="row">Max</th><td>37,627,783</td></tr>
            <tr><th scope="row">Mean</th><td>4,742,066</td></tr>
          </tbody>
        </table>
      <p class="src-note">The 2026-09-12 snapshot mean of 4,742,066 tokens works out to about __MEASURED_SNAPSHOT_DELIVERIES__ deliveries per Pro's __INCLUDED_TOKENS__ tokens. The Cloud pricing page uses about __MEASURED_LARGE_CODEBASE_DELIVERIES__ deliveries because it was measured later on large-codebase deliveries; the samples contain different task sizes. See <a href="/cloud/#pricing">Cloud pricing</a> for the current plan number.</p>
      <p class="src-note">Source, so anyone can re-derive it: the agent session logs of the orbi-build/orbi repository's git worktrees (<code>&lt;repo&gt;/.worktrees/*/.pi-session/*.jsonl</code>), aggregated 2026-09-12. One delivery = one worktree's implement + review sessions; a delivery's totalTokens = the sum of <code>usage.totalTokens</code> over every logged record; n = worktrees whose logs carry at least one usage record (older or newer sessions without usage logging are not countable); percentiles by nearest rank. The sample moves as worktrees are cleaned up. Where the tokens go: <strong>95.9% cache reads, 3.4% input, 0.7% output.</strong></p>
    </section>

    <section class="compare-section compare-section-tint" aria-labelledby="money-title">
      <div class="shell">
        <p class="section-tag">WHAT THAT MEANS IN MONEY</p>
        <h2 class="orbi-compare-section-h2" id="money-title">Cents per delivery (including unmerged work) at DeepSeek V4.1 Flash list prices</h2>
        <p class="section-lede">DeepSeek publishes its prices — <code>deepseek-flash</code> (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash): off-peak, a cache hit is <strong>$0.003/1M</strong> tokens, a cache miss <strong>$0.15/1M</strong>, output <strong>$0.60/1M</strong>. Peak hours (01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 UTC, weekdays) are exactly double. The old sample's mean works out to about <strong>$0.06–0.12 per delivery</strong>. Apply those list prices to the measured distribution:</p>
        <div class="compare-table-wrap">
          <table class="compare-table table-stack">
            <thead><tr><th scope="col">Scenario</th><th scope="col">Off-peak</th><th scope="col">Peak</th></tr></thead>
            <tbody>
              <tr><th scope="row">One delivery (mean, 4.74M tokens)</th><td data-label="Off-peak">$0.058</td><td data-label="Peak">$0.115</td></tr>
              <tr><th scope="row">One delivery (max observed, 37.6M tokens)</th><td data-label="Off-peak">$0.46</td><td data-label="Peak">$0.92</td></tr>
              <tr><th scope="row">100 issues (mean mix)</th><td data-label="Off-peak">~$5.77</td><td data-label="Peak">~$11.55</td></tr>
            </tbody>
          </table>
        </div>
        <p class="src-note">Money computed at the measured token mix (95.9% / 3.4% / 0.7%) against DeepSeek's published deepseek-flash list prices — <a class="orbi-src-note-a" href="https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing" rel="noopener">api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing</a>, verified 2026-09-11.</p>
      </div>
    </section>

    <section class="compare-section shell" aria-labelledby="limits-title">
      <p class="section-tag">READ THE LIMITS FIRST</p>
      <h2 class="orbi-compare-section-h2" id="limits-title">Three things this page does not claim</h2>
      <ul class="event-list">
        <li class="orbi-event-list-li">
          <span class="event-era">OUR REPO ONLY</span>
          <div>
            <strong >This is our repository's measured range — not a promise to everyone</strong>
            <p class="orbi-event-list-p">Python, a full CI suite, and issues written to spec keep our context short. A repository with longer context, slower tests, or vaguer issues lands elsewhere in the distribution. Treat the tables above as what they are: our repo's measured range.</p>
          </div>
        </li>
        <li class="orbi-event-list-li">
          <span class="event-era">CACHING IS LOAD-BEARING</span>
          <div>
            <strong >95.9% cache reads assumes the provider supports prompt caching</strong>
            <p class="orbi-event-list-p">The whole cost structure rests on cache hits. On an endpoint without prompt caching — where every token bills as a miss — the same work costs roughly an order of magnitude more. Check your provider before extrapolating.</p>
          </div>
        </li>
        <li class="orbi-event-list-li">
          <span class="event-era">TOTAL TOKENS, AS BILLED</span>
          <div>
            <strong >Numbers are totalTokens, cache reads included</strong>
            <p class="orbi-event-list-p">That is the line the provider actually bills. Counting only input + output would hide about 96% of the real consumption and flatter the number — the opposite of what this page is for.</p>
          </div>
        </li>
      </ul>
    </section>

    <section class="compare-section shell" aria-labelledby="why-title">
      <p class="section-tag">WHY IT'S SO CHEAP</p>
      <h2 class="orbi-compare-section-h2" id="why-title">A cache hit costs 1/50 of a miss — and 95.9% of the work is cache hits</h2>
      <p class="section-lede">Each delivery re-reads the same repository context: the tree, the conventions, the issue, the failing tests. Prompt caching turns that repeated reading into billed hits at $0.003/1M instead of misses at $0.15/1M. That single ratio is why a full delivery — implementation plus independent review that can repair and rerun — costs cents. It is also the honest question to ask any BYOK agent vendor: <strong>what share of your tokens are cache hits, and what does your provider charge for each?</strong></p>
    </section>

    <section class="compare-section compare-section-tint" aria-labelledby="comparison-title">
      <div class="shell">
        <p class="section-tag">THE $200 TIER, FOR REFERENCE</p>
        <h2 class="orbi-compare-section-h2" id="comparison-title">Competitors quote quotas. We quote tokens and prices.</h2>
        <p class="section-lede">The managed agents at the $200 tier do not publish what your money buys. Verified against their own documentation:</p>
        <ul class="event-list">
          <li class="orbi-event-list-li">
            <span class="event-era">DEVIN</span>
            <div>
              <strong >"A daily and weekly usage quota" — no quantity, no unit price</strong>
              <p class="orbi-event-list-p">Pro ($20/month) includes "a daily and weekly usage quota"; Max ($200/month) adds "a significantly larger weekly usage quota (with no daily cap)". Nowhere on the page does Cognition state how many ACUs either plan includes or what one ACU costs.</p>
              <p class="src-note orbi-event-list-p">Source: <a class="orbi-src-note-a" href="https://docs.devin.ai/admin/billing/self-serve" rel="noopener">docs.devin.ai/admin/billing/self-serve</a> — verified 2026-09-11.</p>
            </div>
          </li>
          <li class="orbi-event-list-li">
            <span class="event-era">FACTORY</span>
            <div>
              <strong >"~5x Pro usage" / "~10x Pro usage" — no absolute values</strong>
              <p class="orbi-event-list-p">Plus ($100/month) is "~5x Pro usage"; Max ($200/month) is "~10x Pro usage". The page states no absolute token quantity and no per-token price anywhere.</p>
              <p class="src-note orbi-event-list-p">Source: <a class="orbi-src-note-a" href="https://docs.factory.ai/pricing/individuals" rel="noopener">docs.factory.ai/pricing/individuals</a> — verified 2026-09-11.</p>
            </div>
          </li>
        </ul>

          <section class="social-proof shell" id="third-party" aria-labelledby="third-party-title">
        <p class="section-tag">THIRD-PARTY RECORDS</p>
        <h2 class="orbi-social-proof-h2" id="third-party-title">Deliveries in other people's repositories</h2>
        <p class="section-lede">Every third-party delivery and quote, grouped by repository: the pull requests Orbi opened in repositories it does not own, and what the people running it said. Newest first.</p>
        <div class="social-proof-group">
          <h3 class="social-proof-group-title">xiaods/k8e</h3>
          <div class="social-proof-grid">
      <article class="proof-card">
